description: Original A1 test draft, independently authored with four options per question. Teacher approval pending.

tabs.title: People and Feelings
tabs.description: Read about Mia and how she feels.

tabs.title: Good Ideas
tabs.description: Use the story to make a choice.

questions.q: Mia sees a word she does not know. How does she feel?
questions.explanation: In paragraph one, Mia reads new words and feels worried.

questions.q: What does Leo do when Mia needs help?
choices: He asks her to try reading again.
questions.explanation: Leo says to read the story again instead of giving all the answers.

questions.q: Why does Mia look at the picture?
choices: It helps her understand a new word.
She wants to draw a train.
It shows the end of the book.
questions.explanation: The picture next to the story helps her understand one word.

questions.q: Why does Mia write a '?' by one sentence?
choices: She wants to write a new story.
She knows the sentence very well.
She needs to ask about that sentence.
She wants to change the train.
questions.explanation: Mia stops at the sentence about a train and marks it with a question mark.

questions.q: Which two people help Mia in the story?
questions.explanation: In paragraph two Leo and her teacher help Mia understand the words.

questions.q: What does Mia want to do after Friday?
questions.explanation: Paragraph three says Mia wants to practise again tomorrow.

questions.q: A friend does not know a word. What can you do like Leo?
choices: Show a picture and help them think.
Ask them to close the book.
questions.explanation: Leo uses the picture to help Mia work out a word.

questions.q: Mia reads a new story on Friday. What is different?
choices: She has no time to read.
questions.explanation: Mia understands more, even though the new story is not easy.

questions.q: Why is Mia happy at the end?
choices: She does not need English now.
She can read better after trying again.
Her brother gives her a new book.
She has no homework on Friday.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph shows Mia understands more and reads to her younger brother.

questions.q: What is a good plan when you cannot read a sentence?
choices: Try again and ask about new words.
questions.explanation: Mia rereads and asks for help with new words, which helps her improve.
